itemList.description:
Specification for Rewinding of 33 kV HT Winding
Supply and complete rewinding of the existing 33 kV HT winding of 3150 kVA, 33/6.6 kV, 3-phase, 50 Hz, ONAN cooled transformer, including dismantling and removal of the existing damaged HT winding, manufacture, supply and installation of new high-conductivity electrolytic copper HT winding, complete with all winding conductors, insulation materials, spacers, end insulation, leads, connections, supporting arrangements, labour, tools, tackles and testing. The HT winding shall be of cross-over type construction with Delta connection, comprising 18 coils per phase, suitable for a rated HT voltage of 33,000 V and rated HT current of 55.112 A at a transformer capacity of 3150 kVA. The winding conductor shall have a minimum cross-sectional area of 8 sq.mm, with bare conductor diameter of 3.19 mm and covered conductor diameter of 3.49 mm, suitable for a phase current of 31.82 A and a current density of approximately 3.98 A/sq.mm. The winding shall be manufactured to suit the existing coil dimensions, with coil I.D. of 427 mm, coil O.D. of 525 mm and coil axial length of 600 mm, with a total of 1308 turns per phase and a resistance per phase at 75 degres C of approximately 1.72801 Ohms. The approximate weight of covered HT conductor shall be 469.73 kg per transformer, subject to actual manufacturing requirements and approved winding design.
The HT winding shall be provided with 0.12 mm mill paper inter-layer insulation between all layers, together with a 2 mm oil duct between the middle layers, exactly in accordance with the existing transformer winding construction. Eight (8) vertical spacers per circle shall be provided in the annular gap between the LV and HV windings. The winding shall be properly supported, compressed and mechanically secured to withstand thermal and short-circuit forces. The HT winding shall be designed to maintain the existing electrical characteristics of the transformer, including 6.25% impedance at full load and 75 degree C, 0.95556 degree resistance at full load and 75 degree C and 6.18% reactance at full load. The rewinding work shall include reconnection of all HT leads to the existing Delta-connected arrangement, proper brazing/soldering of joints as applicable, insulation of all joints and leads, drying, pressing, assembly and vacuum treatment. The quoted rate shall include dismantling, manufacture and installation of the new HT winding, all copper conductor and winding insulation, labour, consumables, testing, transportation within site, handling, and all incidental works required for complete restoration, after deducting the value of recoverable old HT winding copper/material as specified in the tender.
After completion of rewinding, the transformer shall be subjected to all applicable routine and special tests, including insulation resistance test, winding resistance measurement, transformer turns ratio (TTR) test on all taps, vector group/polarity verification, magnetic balance test, impedance measurement, no-load loss and current measurement, load-loss measurement where applicable, dielectric/induced voltage tests, oil BDV test, and other tests prescribed by the relevant IS/IEC standards. Test results shall be submitted to the Engineer-in-Charge for approval before energisation. The contractor shall rectify any defect or failure observed during testing at his own cost.
The contractor shall quote the rate on a complete job basis, inclusive of all labour charges, skilled and unskilled manpower, dismantling and assembly the contractor shall clearly include  the deduction/value considered for the old winding material in the price schedule. No additional payment shall be made for any item required for complete and satisfactory restoration of the transformer unless specifically approved by the Engineer-in-Charge.

Specification for Rewinding of 6.6 kV LV Winding Supply and complete rewinding of the existing 6.6 kV LV winding of 3150 kVA, 33/6.6 kV, 3 phase, 50 Hz, ONAN cooled transformer, including dismantling and removal of the existing damaged LV winding, manufacture, supply and installation of new high-conductivity electrolytic copper LV winding, complete with all conductors, insulation materials, spacers, end insulation, leads, connections, supporting arrangements, labour, tools, tackles and testing. The LV winding shall be of layer-type construction with STAR connection, comprising 4 layers per phase, suitable for a rated LV voltage of 6600 V and rated LV current of 275.55 A at a transformer capacity of 3150 kVA.The winding conductor shall have a minimum cross-sectional area of 108.78 sq.mm, with bare conductor size of 7.7 mm multuiply 2.4 mm, 6 conductors in parallel, and covered conductor size of 8.1 mm multiply  2.8 mm, suitable for a phase current of 275.55 A and a current density of approximately 2.53 A sqmm.The winding shall be manufactured to suit the existing coil dimensions, with coil I.D.of 321 mm, coil O.D. of 397 mm and coil axial length of 640 mm, with a total of 151 turns per phase and resistance per phase at 75 degree C of approximately 0.011067Ohms. The approximate weight of covered LV conductor shall be 519.75 kg per transformer, subject to actual manufacturing requirements and approved winding design.The LV winding shall be provided with 0.45 mm mill paper inter-layer insulation between all adjacent layers, together with a 2.5 mm oil duct between the middle layers, in accordance with the existing transformer winding construction. Eight 8 vertical spacers per circle shall be provided in the annular gap between the LV and HV windings. The winding shall be properly supported, compressed and mechanically secured to withstand thermal, electrical and short-circuit stresses. The rewound LV winding shall maintain the existing STAR -connected arrangement and shall be properly connected to the neutral and associated leads. The work shall include manufacture and installation of the complete LV winding, connection of all internal leads, proper insulation and securing of joints, drying, pressing, assembly and vacuum treatment, together with all necessary testing. The quoted rate shall include dismantling, supply and installation of all copper conductor and winding insulation materials,labour, consumables, testing and all incidental works required for complete restoration, after deducting the value of recoverable old LV winding copper/material as specified in the tender.. Test results shall be submitted to the Engineer-in-Charge for approval before energisation. The contractor shall rectify any defect or failure observed during testing at his own cost.After completion of rewinding, the transformer shall be subjected to all applicable routine and special tests, including insulation resistance test, winding resistance measurement, transformer turns ratio TTR test on all taps, vector group/polarity verification, magnetic balance test The contractor shall quote the rate on a complete job basis, inclusive of all labour charges, skilled and unskilled manpower, dismantling and assembly the contractor shall clearly include  the deduction/value considered for the old winding material in the price schedule. No additional payment shall be made for any item required for complete and satisfactory restoration of the transformer unless specifically approved by the Engineer in Charge

Specification for Insulation System 
The complete rewinding of the transformer shall be carried out using an insulationsystem conforming to the existing manufacturer's design, with Class-A insulation and suitable transformer-grade electrical insulation materials. The primary/HT winding insulation shall be DPC and the secondary/LV winding insulation shall be TPC, with craft paper turn insulation provided on both the HT and LV windings. Suitable pressed compressed-board insulation shall be provided between the core and LV winding and between the HV and LV windings as per the existing construction. The HT winding shall have 0.12 mm mill paper inter-layer insulation between all layers with a 2 mm duct between the middle layers, while the LV winding shall have 0.45 mm mill paper inter-layer insulation between all layers with a 2.5 mm duct between the middle layers. The number and method of application of turn insulation shall be as per the original approved winding design; no arbitrary additional number of paper wraps shall be introduced without approval. All insulation materials shall be new, clean, dry, free from moisture and suitable for transformer oil impregnation and the specified electrical and thermal stresses.All insulation clearances, ducts, spacers, end insulation and lead arrangements shall be inspected and approved before closing the transformer tank and filling with transformer oil. All clearances shall be maintained strictly in accordance with the existing transformer design. The minimum external air clearance shall be 350 mm between HV phase-to-phase, 320 mm between HV phase-to-earth, 255 mm between LV phase-to-phase and 140 mm between LV phase-to-earth. The minimum internal oil clearances shall be 25 mm between the outer surface of the HT winding and the inside of the transformer tank, 40 mm between the outer surface of the HT winding and the tank inside surface where applicable to the HV/LV bushing side arrangement, 85 mm between the HV winding and yokes/end insulation, and 8 mm between the LV winding and yokes/end insulation. The clearance from the top of the yoke to the inside of the top cover of the tank, including gasket, shall be maintained at 114 mm. The minimum clearance between the LT/HT lead arrangement shall be maintained at 15 mm, the radial clearance between the core and LV bare conductor shall be 9 mm, and the phase-to-phase clearance between HV conductors/limbs shall be 15 mm, with a minimum of 2 layers of 1 mm pressboard insulation over the tie rods. The minimum clearance of the core channels from the tank walls shall be maintained at approximately 90 mm at the specified locations, with all clearances verified during assembly. The insulation system shall also satisfy the specified transformer insulation levels of 170 kVp/60 kVp impulse withstand, 70 kV RMS/20 kV RMS power-frequency withstand, and induced over-voltage withstand of 66 kV RMS at 100 Hz on the HV side and 13.2 kV RMS at 100 Hz on the LV side, as applicable.

Supply, filling and commissioning of new inhibited transformer oil conforming to IS 335 2018 (latest amendments/revisions) for the existing 3150 kVA, 33/6.6 kV, 3-phase, 50 Hz, ONAN cooled transformer, complete in all respects.The transformer oil shall be clear and transparent and free from suspended matter, sediments and visible contaminants and shall conform to all applicable physical, chemical, electrical and ageing characteristics specified in IS 335 2018. The oil shall have a maximum density of 0.895 g per ml at 29.5degree C, minimum flash point as specified in IS 335 2018, maximum pour point appropriate to the specified transformer operating conditions, and shall be non corrosive. The minimum breakdown voltage of new, untreated oil shall be 30 kV RMS with 2.5 mm electrode gap, and after filtration per treatment the oil shall achieve the dielectric strength specified under IS 335:2018. The dielectric dissipation factor at 90 degree C, resistivity/specific resistance at 90degree C, acidity, water content, sludge, oxidation stability and all other parameters shall conform to the applicable limits of IS 335 2018. . Approximately 2,300 litres of new transformer oil shall be supplied, or such quantity as is actually required to fill the transformer, conservator and associated oil-filled components up to the manufacturers specified operating oil level.the quoted rate shall include supply of oil, freight, loading, unloading, storage, handling, heating, filtration, dehydration, vacuum treatment, pumping and final filling, including any additional quantity required for topping-up to the prescribed level. Oil samples shall be tested before and after filtration/filling for BDV and other applicable parameters, and satisfactory test results shall be submitted to the Engineer-in-Charge before energisation.The scope shall also include supply and installation of all necessary bus-bar connections, tap leads, connecting lugs, SB rods, gaskets, seals, washers, terminal connectors and other accessories required for complete commissioning of the transformer. The contractor shall undertake loading, unloading and shifting/handling of the transformer using a suitable-capacity Hydra crane, transportation within the site, proper positioning, alignment, levelling and fixing of the transformer on the existing transformer bed/foundation, including all necessary mechanical and electrical connections. Before charging, the contractor shall carry out all required pre-commissioning tests, including insulation resistance, winding resistance, transformer turns ratio on all taps, vector group/polarity verification, oil BDV, oil level, earthing continuity, tap-position verification, protection circuit checks and other applicable tests as per relevant IS/IEC standards. After satisfactory completion of all tests and approval of the Engineer-in-Charge, the transformer shall be charged initially under no-load condition and observed for abnormal noise, vibration, temperature rise, oil leakage, abnormal indications and protection operation. Thereafter, the transformer shall be progressively loaded and its performance shall be observed ON LOAD, including voltage, current, temperature, oil level, protection system and other relevant operating parameters, and the contractor shall ensure satisfactory performance at rated load. Any defect, abnormality or deficiency observed during testing, energisation or loading shall be rectified by the contractor at his own cost. The quoted rate shall be complete in all respects, inclusive of transformer oil, filtration and dehydration, all materials and accessories, labour, testing, vacuum equipment, Hydra/crane charges, freight, loading and unloading, installation, testing, commissioning and all incidental works necessary for successful and satisfactory commissioning of the transformer, with no additional payment for any item required for complete operation.
